---
title: "Before the day"
---

Before the day, install R and the IDE workspace, work through the first module on R, and read the background page. The day assumes that a linear model and its output are not new to you.

## 1. R and the IDE workspace {#the-workspace}

[Install R and an IDE](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Download the IDE workspace]({{< var cases.europeanisation.workspace-zip >}}){.btn .btn-primary}

Install R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) by the steps of the setup page of the AR4DS website, and download the IDE workspace of the case study.

{{< include ../../_includes/_workspace.qmd >}}

The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. If the installation fails, tell the facilitator before the day.

## 2. Getting started with R

[Open Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work through the module, whose blocks of code run in your browser.

## 3. Background {#the-case-study}

[Read the background](../../background.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The background page presents the claim on which the day works and the five reanalyses of it in the SCORE robustness study (Aczel et al. 2026).

## 4. The slides and the webR workspace {#the-deck-and-the-browser-lab}

[Open the slides at Task 1](../../live/day.html#/hands-on-1-get-yourself-running){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the webR workspace at Task 1](../../lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The slides used on the day and the webR workspace run R inside your browser, and they are the fallback if your installation fails. Open the slides once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the cells on their slide of the setup check show a "Run Code" button, and run them. The second should report 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years. If the slides do not load, try the webR workspace or another browser.

## 5. Further preparation

Optional readings: the first sections of [Panel data](../../companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-aggregation), from the country-year level to clustered standard errors, [the reading on inference](../../curve.qmd#inference) of the Specification curve page for Part 4, and [the readings on preregistration](../../resources.qmd#preregistration) on the Resources page for Task 5. The modules on [the IDE (Positron and other IDEs)](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), on [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and on [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) take the tools of the IDE workspace further.

## 6. On the day

Bring a laptop with the IDE workspace working on it. The day needs no account of any kind, whether for Git and GitHub, the OSF, a data archive or an AI assistant, and every tool that it uses is free.
